issues.legal_issue: A custodian administering property held for an evacuee may consider and pay a creditor’s claim from the administered funds when the claimant is found entitled and payment serves the administration of the property.
material_facts: The claimant held money decrees against a debtor whose property had vested in the custodian.
Execution against the property was unavailable while it remained vested in the custodian.
The claimant applied for payment from the administered estate, but the application was rejected on the ground that the custodian lacked power to grant relief.
The tribunals had not decided whether the claim was genuine, whether the claimant was entitled to payment, or whether payment should be made for the purposes of administration.
issues.conclusion: The custodian had power, coupled with a duty to exercise that power, to consider the claim and to pay it if the custodian was satisfied that the claimant was entitled and payment served the statutory purposes of administration. The rejection orders were set aside and the matter remanded for that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(1) gives the custodian general powers to secure, administer, preserve, and manage evacuee property and to discharge duties under the Act. Section 10(2)(n) permits payment from funds in the custodian’s possession to the evacuee, a family member, or any other person whom the custodian considers entitled. Administration includes discharging obligations binding on the evacuee, not merely collecting and managing assets. The clauses of section 10(2) illustrate, and are not mutually exclusive limits on, the general powers in section 10(1). No earlier cases are relied upon in the judgment.

predicates.claim_for_payment_from_administered_prop: A claimant asks the administrator of property held for an absent owner to pay a monetary claim from that property.
predicates.property_held_for_evacuee: The property whose funds are sought is held by an administrator for an evacuee.
predicates.claimant_found_entitled: The administrator determines that the claimant is entitled to receive the claimed money.
predicates.payment_serves_property_administration: The administrator determines that paying the claim serves the administration or management of the property or the discharge of the administrator’s duties.

issues.definition: When a payment claim concerns property held for an evacuee, the custodian may pay it from the administered funds if the claimant is found entitled or payment serves the administration of the property.

issues.legal_issue: Removing an express power to pay an evacuee’s debts does not eliminate an independent power to pay a person found entitled to money from the administered estate.
material_facts: The Act originally expressly authorized expenditure for debts due by an evacuee, and a rule provided a procedure for registering claims.
An amendment deleted the express reference to payment of evacuee debts, and the rule providing the claim-registration procedure was later deleted.
The claimant sought payment under the separate provision permitting payment to any other person whom the custodian considered entitled.
The tribunals rejected the claim for lack of power without deciding its merits.
issues.conclusion: The deletion of the express debt-payment language and the claim-registration rule did not remove the custodian’s independent power under section 10(1) and section 10(2)(n) to consider and pay qualifying claims.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(1) states the custodian’s general powers and duties, while section 10(2)(n) permits payment to any other person considered entitled. The specific clauses are illustrative and not mutually exclusive. The deletion from section 10(2)(m) of the express reference to evacuee debts and the deletion of Rule 22 did not restrict the separate authority under section 10(1) and section 10(2)(n). No earlier cases are relied upon in the judgment.

predicates.claim_for_payment_from_administered_prop: A claimant asks the administrator of property held for an absent owner to pay a monetary claim from that property.
predicates.express_debt_payment_authority_removed: An express authorization for the administrator to pay the absent owner’s debts has been removed.
predicates.independent_authority_to_pay_entitled_pe: A separate continuing authorization allows the administrator to pay a person whom the administrator considers entitled to money from the administered funds.

issues.definition: If a payment claim is made after an express debt-payment authorization is removed, a separate continuing authority to pay persons found entitled preserves the administrator’s power to consider and pay the claim.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court decree does not conclusively establish a claimant’s entitlement to payment from property administered for an evacuee, and the custodian must assess the claim judicially rather than arbitrarily.
material_facts: The claimant relied on money decrees against the evacuee to seek payment from funds held by the custodian.
The tribunals had not assessed whether the claim was genuine or whether the claimant was entitled to payment.
The Supreme Court remanded the matter for the custodian to form an opinion on entitlement and payment.
issues.conclusion: The decree was not decisive of entitlement to payment from the administered funds. The custodian had to determine the claim’s genuineness and the claimant’s entitlement, acting judicially and not arbitrarily.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(n), entitlement is a matter for the custodian’s opinion, but that opinion does not confer arbitrary authority. The custodian must consider the circumstances and determine the claim judicially. A civil or revenue court decree or other authority’s order is not decisive of the claim against the evacuee property. No earlier cases are relied upon in the judgment.

predicates.claim_for_payment_from_administered_prop: A claimant asks the administrator of property held for an absent owner to pay a monetary claim from that property.
predicates.claim_supported_by_court_decree: The claimant relies on a court decree as support for the payment claim.

issues.definition: When a payment claim against administered property is supported by a court decree, the custodian must still assess entitlement independently and judicially.

issues.legal_issue: Property vested in a custodian for an evacuee cannot be proceeded against in execution while it remains so vested.
material_facts: The debtor’s property had vested in the custodian after the debtor was declared an evacuee.
The claimant had sought to execute money decrees against the property, and the custodian obtained removal of an attachment.
The property remained vested in the custodian when the claimant sought payment from the custodian instead.
issues.conclusion: While the property remained vested in the custodian, it was not liable to be proceeded against in execution of a decree or order; the claimant could not execute against it and instead applied to the custodian for payment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1) bars recourse to evacuee property vested in the custodian through execution of a decree or order of a court or other authority while the property remains vested. The bar applies whether the claim is against the evacuee or arises from acts of administration by the custodian. No earlier cases are relied upon in the judgment.

predicates.execution_proceeding_against_administere: A creditor seeks to enforce a decree or order through execution against property held by an administrator for an evacuee.
predicates.property_remains_vested_in_custodian: The property continues to be vested in the custodian when execution is sought.

issues.definition: Execution against property held for an evacuee is prohibited when the property remains vested in the custodian.
